x: Burning fossil fuels and deforestation release the most CO2 and destroy carbon sinks; wind, solar power and planting trees reduce warming.

x: 'Anthropocene' (human epoch) is the name proposed for the epoch of human impact; the Holocene is the current official epoch, Neocene/Manocene are not proposals.

x: Water vapour is the biggest overall contributor to the greenhouse effect; CO2 is the main human-emitted GHG, which is the trap when water vapour is not offered.
source: Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.8; NextGen Rocket Environment p.13

x: The Paris Agreement aims to keep warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.12; NCERT Physical Geography (OnlyIAS) Part 8 p.9

x: The greenhouse effect is the warming effect of GHGs that trap outgoing heat; it is not cooling, extra rainfall or desertification.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.7; NextGen Rocket Environment p.13

x: The primary cause of present global warming is the increase in GHG concentrations; deforestation adds to it, and ozone depletion is a separate problem.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.12; Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.6-7

x: Carbon footprint = total GHGs (CO2) emitted by a person's, organisation's or product's activities, in tonnes per year.
Sodium hydroxide is a chemical (alkali), not a GHG; water vapour, nitrous oxide and CO2 are GHGs.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment p.13; NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.7

x: No level of warming is proven 'safe'; Paris uses 1.5°C and 2°C as limits, which is the tempting option.
source: printed key, not verified; NextGen Rocket Environment p.14 (Paris limits)
dispute: Printed key: 'No one knows'. Some keys / the Copenhagen-Paris guardrail: 2°C (UPSC 2014 stem: 'should not exceed 2°C') (NextGen Rocket Environment p.14).

x: Floods are disasters triggered indirectly by human action (deforestation, encroachment) acting through natural processes; wars and pollution are direct human actions.
The greenhouse effect is a naturally occurring warming of Earth's surface and lower atmosphere (I); it has nothing to do with biodegradable waste in water, which causes eutrophication (II).
source: Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.7; NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.7

x: Global warming means a gradual increase in the Earth's average atmospheric temperature.

A, C and D are true: water vapour, CFCs and HFCs are GHGs and fossil fuels, deforestation and livestock add GHGs. B is false – the effect comes from absorbing long-wave infrared emitted by Earth, not short-wave radiation.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.8; NextGen Rocket Environment p.13

x: A gradual rise in the average temperature of the atmosphere and oceans that is changing climate is global warming.
GHGs warm the atmosphere by trapping (absorbing and re-radiating) heat emitted by the surface; they do not generate heat.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.7; NextGen Rocket Environment p.13

x: Humans do not emit enough water vapour to change its level directly; they raise it indirectly, because warmer air (from other GHGs) holds more water vapour.
Greenhouse gases absorb and re-radiate Earth's outgoing heat and warm the surface; the ozone layer absorbs UV, and currents and winds only move heat.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.7; NextGen Rocket Environment p.13

x: The greenhouse effect means an increase in global (atmospheric) temperature caused by GHGs, not warming of seawater or rivers alone.
The surface re-emits long-wave infrared rays, which GHGs absorb; UV, gamma and X-rays are not involved.
Commonly keyed 'all of the above': GHGs are the main cause; ozone depletion and pollution (aerosols, black carbon) also alter climate.
source: printed key, not verified; Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.6-7

x: The greenhouse concept was first proposed by Joseph Fourier in the 1820s.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment p.13; NextGen Rocket Environment p.58

x: Burning fossil fuels produces mainly CO2; methane and N2O come mostly from farming, and ozone is a secondary gas.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.8; Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.8-10

x: Greenhouse effect = rise in atmospheric temperature due to the concentration of GHGs, not growing plants in glass houses.
Keyed as 'increase in CO2 concentration': the enhanced greenhouse effect goes with rising CO2 in the atmosphere. Warming also raises humidity, but that is a consequence, not the textbook answer.
source: printed key, not verified; NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.7
dispute: Printed key / most books: increase in CO2 concentration. Strictly, rising CO2 causes the enhanced effect, and the change the effect itself brings is warming and more water vapour (humidity) (Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.8).

x: The greenhouse effect warms the lower atmosphere (surface and troposphere), where GHGs trap outgoing heat.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.7 ('warm the air in the lower levels'); Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.7

x: The atmosphere is heated mainly by long-wave terrestrial radiation from the earth, not directly by short-wave or reflected solar radiation.
Fresh snow has the highest albedo, reflecting about 80-85% of sunlight – far more than sand, paddy or prairie.
Clouds stop heat radiating away from the ground at night and send part of it back, so cloudy nights are warmer.
Only statement 2: of 35 units reflected, 27 come from cloud tops – about one-fourth. Statement 1 is wrong: the surface re-emits heat as long-wave infrared, not ultraviolet.
The atmosphere gets its warmth indirectly from the earth's long-wave terrestrial radiation, not mainly from short-wave solar radiation.

II and III are correct: heat trapped by the atmosphere maintains the average temperature, and CO2 absorbs long-wave radiation well. I is too sweeping – without an atmosphere the day side would be very hot, like the Moon, though the average would be about −18°C.
source: PMF IAS PYQ 2025 (search result, page blocked); NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.8
evidence: web search: superkalam.com, examday.ai, superpathshala.com give (c); PMF IAS gives (d)
dispute: Many coaching keys: (c) I, II and III (Statement I taken as broadly true). Strictly: I is wrong – an airless Earth would swing between very hot days and frozen nights (PMF IAS); the printed key (d) follows this.

x: Statement I is wrong – the atmosphere is heated more by terrestrial (long-wave) radiation than by incoming solar radiation; Statement II is right – CO2 and other GHGs absorb long-wave radiation well.
Increasing order of contribution: N2O (~5-6%) < methane (~20%) < CO2 (~60%), i.e. II-I-III.
CO2 is the major GHG driving present climate change, ahead of methane, N2O and ozone.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment p.13; Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.8-10

x: Reducing GHG emissions for environmental sustainability is a principle in international conventions; the rest put growth before environment.
Optimum hatchability needs CO2 kept low, about 0.3-0.5% in the incubator; higher levels cut hatchability.
Acid rain is caused mainly by high SO2 (with NOx) that forms sulphuric and nitric acids; ozone depletion, UV-B and GHGs are not its cause.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 5.2 p.3 (sulphur oxides cause acid rain)

x: Among the options CO2 contributes most to the greenhouse effect; H2S is not a GHG, and N2O and methane contribute less.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment p.13; NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.10

x: Water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas in the atmosphere.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment p.13; NextGen Rocket Environment p.58

x: Nitrous oxide (laughing gas) is used as a weak anaesthetic; CO, mercury vapour and ammonia are toxic.
Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the greenhouse gas known as laughing gas.
CO2 and other gases absorbing the heat that bounces off (is re-radiated by) the earth cause global warming; acid rain comes from SO2/NOx.
Nitrous oxide is laughing gas; SO2, helium and CO are not.
CO2 makes the highest contribution to total global warming (~60%), ahead of methane, N2O and CFCs.
Only methane is a GHG; carbon monoxide is only an indirect GHG.

x: Only CO2 is a GHG; SO2 causes acid rain and is not a GHG.
Both CO2 and methane are greenhouse gases.

x: Methane is the second most important anthropogenic GHG after CO2 (~20% of enhanced warming).
Tropospheric ozone, methane and nitrous oxide are all GHGs; ammonia, lead, aerosols and methanol are not.
source: NextGen Rocket Environment p.13; NextGen Rocket Environment p.57

x: Industrial Revolution (C) → rising GHG emissions (B) → Kyoto Protocol signed 1997 (E) → heightened concern about warming (A) → Paris Agreement 2015 (D); it is the only option with C first and Kyoto before Paris.
source: printed key, not verified; NextGen Rocket Environment p.14

x: Both true: the greenhouse effect is natural and heats the surface and atmosphere, and CO2 and methane are the common GHGs.
source: Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.7; NextGen Rocket Environment p.13

x: Di-nitrogen (N2) does not absorb infrared and is not a GHG; CO2, methane and ozone are.
Methane is a GHG; nitrogen, oxygen and argon are not.
CO2 and methane are the main GHGs; ammonia, CO and SO2 are not, and CF4 is not the paired answer.
Global warming is expected to make the Indian monsoon more erratic and extreme (devastating and unpredictable).
Ascending GWP: CO2 (1) < methane (21-36) < N2O (~300) < HFCs (up to ~11,700).
Nitrogen (78% of air) does not absorb infrared and is not a GHG; CO2, N2O and water vapour are.
Calcium carbonate is a solid mineral, not a gas; methane and CO2 are major GHGs and CO an indirect one.
All three warm the atmosphere: soot (black carbon) absorbs radiation, SF6 is the most potent GHG, and water vapour is the most abundant GHG (UPSC key d).

x: Flooded rice paddies emit methane (anaerobic decay) and fertilised paddy soils emit N2O, so rice is the main anthropogenic source of both.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.8; NextGen Rocket Environment p.57

x: Argon is an inert gas and not a GHG; methane, water vapour and CO2 are.

CO2 and methane are GHGs responsible for warming; oxygen is not a GHG.
Nitrogen is not a GHG; CO2, methane and N2O are.
CO2 is the main component of human GHG forcing – about 66% (WMO).

Water vapour causes the highest share of the natural greenhouse effect (about half).
source: Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.8; NextGen Rocket Environment p.13

x: Rice paddies are the main anthropogenic source of both methane and N2O.
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.1 p.8; NextGen Rocket Environment p.57

x: Propane is a fuel, not a GHG; CO2, methane and ozone are GHGs.

Flooded paddy fields release methane under anaerobic conditions.
Argon is not a GHG; CFCs, CO2 and methane are.
Oxygen does not absorb infrared and is not a GHG.

x: Oxides of sulphur and nitrogen do not warm the climate directly; methane, CO2 and water vapour are GHGs.

x: CO2, methane, nitrous oxide and water vapour are the most important GHGs; chlorine, ethane, CO and SO2 are not.

x: Paddy fields produce methane (about 50-100 million t a year).

Hydrogen is not a GHG; methane, N2O and CFCs are.
CO2 and methane are responsible for global warming; O2 is not a GHG.
CO2 has the highest contribution to global warming.

x: Water vapour is the most abundant GHG; SO2 is not a GHG.
CO2 and methane contribute to the greenhouse effect; CO and SO2 are not GHGs and NH3 is not one.

Methane is commonly called marsh gas; laughing gas is N2O.
Among CFCs, N2O, CO2 and methane, CO2 has by far the largest concentration (~420 ppm).
CO2 and methane contribute to the greenhouse effect; the other pairs include non-GHGs.
Soot, SF6 and water vapour all warm the atmosphere.

x: False statement: CFCs are GHGs as well as ozone-depleting.

Oxygen is not a GHG; CO2 and CH4 are.

x: Flooded low-land rice is anaerobic, so methane is the main GHG it releases.

Rice fields, coal mining, domestic animals (human) and wetlands (natural) are all methane sources.
Singapore announced (Feb 2018) a carbon tax from 2019 under its Paris commitments.
All four are methane sources (wetlands are the largest natural one).
All four are methane sources.
Fossil-fuel burning, oil-driven automobiles and deforestation cause climate change; solar flares are not a primary cause.
Both: anaerobic paddies emit methane and nitrogen fertilisers release N2O from soil.

Statements 1, 2 and 4 are causes; increasing solar flares is not.
Beyond 3°C the land biosphere turns into a net carbon source and widespread coral mortality occurs; total loss of wetlands and of cereals everywhere is exaggerated (UPSC key b).
Only I and II: biosphere becomes a carbon source and corals die widely; III and IV are extreme claims.
Black carbon is a short-lived pollutant from incomplete combustion; it is not methane, not from CFCs and does not deplete ozone.

x: Printed key: 'long-term change' is not an indicator; floral (plant fossils), cryogenic (glaciation) and tectonic (continental drift) indicators are.

x: Deforestation raises CO2 and causes loss of biodiversity – both.
Both consequences are correct.
All three contribute: burning coal and petroleum, deforestation and methane from animal waste.
The greenhouse effect increases Earth's temperature.
Public transport, less use of refrigerants and afforestation all reduce warming.
Himalayan glaciers such as Gangotri are melting because of global warming (driven by GHGs).
Incorrect statement: deforestation increases CO2, it does not decrease it.
A-1 (global warming – rising seas), B-3 (air pollution – respiratory illness), C-2 (sub-regional temperature – patches of cooling), D-4 (habitat loss – extinction).
Melting glaciers, sea-level rise, weather changes and rising temperature all indicate global warming.
Melting glaciers, early flowering of mango and health impacts are effects; better global communication is not.
All four are impacts of global warming.
Rising seas change coastlines and warming alters crop patterns – all of the above.
Both are Paris goals: well below 2°C (A) and pursue efforts toward 1.5°C (B).
COP21 Paris set the limit at 2°C above pre-industrial levels (well below 2°C, aiming for 1.5°C).
Social cost of carbon = money value of the long-term damage from one tonne of CO2 emitted in a given year.
DAC pulls CO2 from ambient air: it serves sequestration, supplies CO2 for plastics and food processing, and gives carbon for synthetic aviation fuel – all three.
The glass sheet of a solar cooker lets sunlight in and traps long-wave heat, like a greenhouse.
Oceansat-2 (2009) carries an ocean colour monitor and scatterometer: water vapour/winds, monsoon onset and coastal pollution – all three (UPSC 2010).
The UK Parliament was the first national parliament to declare a climate emergency, on 1 May 2019.

x: As oceans warm, marine fish shift towards the poles (cooler waters).
a-iv (CO2 uptake – falling pH), b-ii (melting Arctic ice – more surface CO2), c-iii (plankton blooms – bacterial respiration, eutrophication), d-i (less carbonate – less neutralising ability).
source: NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.2 p.7-8; Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.17

x: Snails, sea urchins and oysters all build calcium carbonate shells, so all are at risk.
Honeybees perform the waggle dance to show direction and distance of food (Karl von Frisch).
I, II and III (UPSC key a): less carbonate harms calcareous phytoplankton, coral reefs and animals with phytoplanktonic larvae. IV (clouds) is not in the official key.
source: Shankar Environment 15 (OCR) p.17; NextGen Environment APPSC Part 8.2 p.7-8
dispute: Official UPSC key / most books: I, II and III. NextGen Environment Part 8.2 p.8 notes that acidified water cuts DMS from phytoplankton and may reduce cloud formation, which would also support IV.

x: Biorock (mineral accretion) technology is used to restore damaged coral reefs.
DSV Limiting Factor was carried by the support ship DSSV Pressure Drop ('Prizer drop' is a misprint) in the Five Deeps Expedition.
